title: Aurora ML Pilot — Weekly Cost & Tuning
summary: Weekly POC sync to review token economics and tuning experiments. Reviewed tokens/sec/$ baselines, caching hit improvements, and batching tradeoffs. Agreed on next tuning steps: increase KV/prefix cache retention, try hybrid batching (dynamic batch up to 8), and run a focused latency-sensitive benchmark for p95 SLA. Follow-ups: updated cost model sheet, revised pilot config, schedule throughput window.
action_items: Emma Clarke: Send revised pilot config (cache + batching) by 2025-07-11
Ravi Patel: Prepare 15-min p95 latency benchmark run and script by 2025-07-13
Diego Ramos: Provide real-world prompt distribution sample (1k prompts) by 2025-07-12
next_steps: Redwood to push updated pilot YAML with cacheTTL=600s and dynamic_batch_max=8
Customer to approve a 2-hour throughput window next week (prefer Tues 07/15) for p95 tests
Redwood to update cost projection spreadsheet with new cache-hit assumptions and share annotated version
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-09 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Emma Clarke (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (CTO - Aurora ML), Diego Ramos (ML Engineer), Priya Nair (Infra)

Auto-summary (auto): quick economic deep dive + tuning list.

[00:00] Emma Clarke: All right, good afternoon everyone, thanks for carving out time. Quick check in — is this still the weekly pilot sync for Aurora?
[00:12] Lena Ortiz: yes, yep this is good, thanks. Diego and I are here. Priya might jump in a bit later.
[00:20] Ravi Patel: Cool. Agenda today, tokens per dollar baseline, cache numbers from last run, and then batching experiments and impact on p95. Any additional items?
[00:28] Lena Ortiz: maybe a quick note on the on-prem infra ergonomics, but keep it short.

[02:05] Ravi Patel: Ok starting with the baseline: last week we ran model variant A (we'll call it l2-13b-q4) on Redwood Dedicated pool. Measured raw throughput at steady state: ~14,800 tokens/sec per GPU node at batch size 1, cost math gave us
[02:22] Diego Ramos: wait, 14.8k tokens/sec per node? that seemed high compared to our earlier runs (we were seeing 9k).
[02:32] Ravi Patel: right so note the difference — your earlier runs used sequence length 512 and this was using shorter median sequences ~120 tokens; the distribution matters a lot. The tokens/sec/$ in our cost sheet right now is 12,000 tokens per dollar for the baseline mix (batch1, no cache).
[02:52] Lena Ortiz: where does that 12k come from? I thought our previous calc said 8k tokens/$ after infra overheads.
[03:02] Emma Clarke: Good callout — the spreadsheet (linked in notes) had two tabs: raw inference cost and infra overheads. The 12k is inference-only; our recommended customer-facing metric includes the infra overhead + dedicated reservation amortization which brings it down to ~8.6k tokens/$, so table uses both.

[05:15] Priya Nair: (joins) Sorry, quick context: our finance needs the tokens per dollar that include network / cloud egress. So please keep that higher-level number.
[05:25] Emma Clarke: noted. We'll propagate the full-cost number in the next sheet.

[06:10] Ravi Patel: Cache results — we enabled prefix caching and KV caching last Thursday for the session that ran with a warm-up period. Hit rate observed: 42% prefix hits and 18% KV hits which combined to approx 46% total token-level savings on average for that workload. That maps to a cost reduction of ~36% in tokens/$ when you apply hit-rate scaling.
[06:37] Diego Ramos: how consistent was that hit-rate? Our production prompt set is pretty bursty, I was worried warm-up would be poor except for a few flows.
[06:45] Ravi Patel: Good question. The hit-rate varied — for the FAQ/generation flows hits were 60-65% but for open-ended assistant prompts it was <10%. The overall 46% is a weighted average using the sample prompt distribution you gave us. If you change distribution (more long-form) the benefit drops.
[07:10] Lena Ortiz: so if we could bias more traffic toward canned responses we get the 36% cost saving, but that's product-level. For the POC we need a conservative number.

[08:05] Emma Clarke: Right — we suggested showing both optimistic (46% hit) and conservative (25% hit) projections. The conservative projection still yields about 18% cost reduction.

[09:30] Ravi Patel: Batching — we tested batch sizes of 1, 4, 8, and dynamic up-to-32. Cost per token decreased with batch size: ~12k tokens/$ at batch=1 -> ~31k tokens/$ at batch=8 (inference-only), but tail latency increases. p95 latencies: batch1 p95 ~120ms, batch8 p95 ~420ms, dynamic-8 p95 ~230ms in our run due to batching window heuristics.
[10:05] Diego Ramos: That p95 jump to 420ms is too big for our UI. We need <=300ms p95 for interactive prompts.
[10:12] Ravi Patel: understood. That's why we proposed hybrid: dynamic batching with max 8 but with latency guard for requests tagged 'interactive' to bypass batching (route to priority lane).
[10:25] Emma Clarke: we can set route tags in the call (metadata) so priority traffic is served with batch=1; background tasks can be batched aggressively. That keeps perceived latency low but still captures batching savings on non-critical traffic.

[12:45] Priya Nair: Any ops complexity to do that on Redwood Dedicated? We run in VPC and our security team prefers minimal routing complexity.
[12:55] Ravi Patel: No extra infra — routing policies live in the control plane. We just need consistent request metadata keys. We'll provide SDK snippet.

[14:02] Lena Ortiz: Let's talk numbers for the hybrid approach — if 30% of traffic is interactive and bypasses batching, and 70% is batched at effective batch 6, what's net tokens/$?
[14:15] Ravi Patel: quick ballpark — using our bench numbers: interactive (batch1) yields 12k tokens/$, batched portion (batch6 approximate) yields 28k tokens/$. Weighted: 0.3*12k + 0.7*28k = 24.8k tokens/$. That's ~2.8x improvement over all-batch1. After infra overhead your customer-facing number will be lower, maybe 1.9x improvement.
[14:45] Diego Ramos: Good. Can we validate that with a run that mimics 30/70 split?
[14:52] Ravi Patel: Yes — that's the focused throughput window we want to run. We'll instrument tags for interactive vs batchable.

[17:30] Emma Clarke: On cache retention — we set TTL 60s in the pilot. Increasing to 600s increased hits in our long-run test, but risk of stale responses for very dynamic prompts. For Aurora's taxonomy, 600s looked safe for FAQ and system prompts.
[17:50] Diego Ramos: I'm concerned about privacy/regulation — cached content might include PII. Are cached tokens encrypted and audit-logged?
[18:00] Ravi Patel: yes — KV/prefix cache entries are encrypted at rest with customer KMS and audit logs tied to the control plane. We'll attach the security note. (slight pause) sometimes the transcript tool says KMS as K-M-S or K-M-Z, apologies.
[18:20] Priya Nair: Good, please send the exact KMS steps to on-board.

[20:10] Ravi Patel: Ok moving to fallback model variants: we tested quantized variant (q4->q8?) sorry q4_0 quant on variant B, which is slightly cheaper per token but quality drop on long-coherence prompts. We recommend canary routing: try cheaper variant for batchable background tasks, keep high-fidelity model for interactive.
[20:45] Lena Ortiz: makes sense. Customer success question — how do we measure quality regressions? We have a set of 200 eval prompts we can run.
[20:55] Emma Clarke: perfect, we'll plug those into Redwood Optimize eval harness and surface quality delta and token delta side-by-side.

[23:05] Diego Ramos: About the cost projection sheet — I noticed numbers in the infra tab didn't include reserved capacity discounts we expect from our procurement (15%).
[23:15] Emma Clarke: we built the sheet flexible — there's a 'discount' cell. If you give us the expected discount we can recalc. For now we used conservative 0% in the public sheet.

[25:12] Ravi Patel: Proposed experiment run list: 1) 2-hour mixed workload with 30/70 interactive/batched tags (throughput + p95) 2) 24-hour cache TTL sweep (60s, 300s, 600s) to measure stability 3) Model-variant canary for background tasks. Which should we prioritize?
[25:35] Lena Ortiz: prioritize 1 and 2. We want the quick win on cost.

[27:40] Priya Nair: Ops note — we can give a reserved maintenance window Tues 07/15 02:00-04:00 UTC. That should be low-traffic for us.
[27:50] Emma Clarke: Great, we'll aim for that.

[30:05] Ravi Patel: Quick nit: we saw some transcription noise in the initial test logs (some token dropping) — that's probably a metrics export bug, not inference bug. We'll fix the logger and reshare raw logs.

[33:20] Diego Ramos: Minor UX ask — can we get a dashboard tile that shows cache hit-rate and effective tokens/$ in near real-time?
[33:28] Emma Clarke: yes that's doable — Redwood Console has a per-route KPI tile; we'll add a pre-configured Aurora route tile and share link.

[38:10] Lena Ortiz: Pricing ask — if we run dedicated nodes with autoscale burst, is there a simple estimate for peak vs steady cost?
[38:22] Emma Clarke: In the cost sheet we added a 'peak factor' slider. Example: steady 4 nodes, peak 8 nodes for 10% of time -> blended cost increases by ~18% for that usage profile. We'll annotate the sheet with that sample.

[41:05] Ravi Patel: Quick check on security review items — Priya, anything outstanding that blocks the TTL/cache change?
[41:12] Priya Nair: Just need the KMS integration doc and confirmation that audit logs are retained 90 days.
[41:20] Emma Clarke: We'll attach SOC2+KMS docs in the follow-up.

[46:00] Emma Clarke: Recap — agreed experiments: 2-hour mixed throughput (target Tues 07/15 02:00-04:00 UTC), TTL sweep for 24h after that, and model-variant canary for background tasks. Action owners in the sheet. We'll update cost projection with a conservative and optimistic scenario and push the new pilot YAML (cacheTTL=600, dynamic_batch_max=8) by Friday 07/11.
[46:35] Lena Ortiz: Sounds good. Also please make sure the p95 targets are clearly shown for interactive route.
[46:45] Diego Ramos: I'll upload the 1k prompt sample and the 200-eval set by Friday.

[49:00] Emma Clarke: Anything else?
[49:05] Priya Nair: No, that covers infra concerns.
[49:10] Lena Ortiz: No, thanks everyone.
[49:20] Emma Clarke: Thanks all — we'll follow up with calendar invite and the config change diff.

End transcript.

Shared artifacts referenced: cost sheet, bench notebook, security KMS doc.

Call end.
